measures.title: Vacancy excise tax
measures.change: create the residential vacancy tax and authorize the city to retain and spend its revenue
measures.yes_means: A yes vote would create the residential vacancy tax and authorize the city to retain and spend its revenue.
measures.no_means: A no vote would not create the residential vacancy tax and authorize the city to retain and spend its revenue.
measures.plain: In plain words: bouldervotes.org's summary of the city's ballot information, not the ballot text.

supports.name: Boulder County Democratic Socialists of America

money.text: Ballot language estimates $6 million in 2028, the first full collection year. Initial rate is $4,000 per qualifying vacant home, indexed to inflation but capped at $7,000; actual collections depend on how many homes qualify and whether owners change how they use them. The $6 million figure is a ballot revenue estimate, not a guaranteed collection amount.

measures.title: Building Boulder Together: Recreation and Safety Bond
measures.change: authorize up to $400 million in general-obligation debt and a property-tax levy to repay it, within the ballot's stated annual tax and total repayment ceilings
measures.yes_means: A yes vote would authorize up to $400 million in general-obligation debt and a property-tax levy to repay it, within the ballot's stated annual tax and total repayment ceilings.
measures.no_means: A no vote would not authorize up to $400 million in general-obligation debt and a property-tax levy to repay it, within the ballot's stated annual tax and total repayment ceilings.
measures.plain: In plain words: bouldervotes.org's summary of the city's ballot information, not the ballot text.

opposes.name: Boulder County Democratic Socialists of America

money.text: Debt cap $400 million, maximum total repayment $650 million, and annual tax increase up to $32.5 million. The city estimates that, if it borrowed the full $400 million, a $1 million residential property would pay about $400 more each year for roughly 20 years; borrowing less or in stages changes the tax impact. The listed project estimates total more than $400 million, so not every estimate is guaranteed to be fully covered by this bond.

measures.title: Collective bargaining for firefighters (new Charter §73)
measures.change: add the specified collective-bargaining right and dispute process to the charter
measures.yes_means: A yes vote would add the specified collective-bargaining right and dispute process to the charter.
measures.no_means: A no vote would not add the specified collective-bargaining right and dispute process to the charter.
measures.plain: In plain words: bouldervotes.org's summary of the city's ballot information, not the ballot text.

supports.name: Boulder County Democratic Socialists of America
Boulder Firefighters for a Stronger Boulder

money.text: The published ballot question has no specific tax, debt, or dollar amount. Future negotiated labor costs are not quantified in the ballot language; an unresolved impasse could lead to an election under the proposed process.

measures.title: Charter debt-limit calculation (actual vs. assessed value)
measures.change: amend the charter's debt-limit calculation to three percent of actual taxable property value
measures.yes_means: A yes vote would amend the charter's debt-limit calculation to three percent of actual taxable property value.
measures.no_means: A no vote would not amend the charter's debt-limit calculation to three percent of actual taxable property value.
measures.plain: In plain words: bouldervotes.org's summary of the city's ballot information, not the ballot text.

opposes.name: Boulder County Democratic Socialists of America

money.text: No direct tax increase or new bond is authorized by this question alone. The city's legal debt ceiling would increase by switching the base from assessed to actual value; the resulting dollar limit depends on taxable property value. A contemporaneous advocacy presentation estimated a change from about $152.7 million to $1.55 billion; treat these as estimates, not official ballot language.

basics.deadline: Ballots must be received (not postmarked) by 7 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The county recommends mailing by October 26; after that, use a drop box or Vote Center.
how_to_vote: Boulder County mails ballots to registered voters starting October 2, 2026. 24-hour drop boxes open the same day.
Ballots must be received (not postmarked) by 7 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The county recommends mailing by October 26; after that, use a drop box or Vote Center.
Vote Centers open October 19 for in-person voting and same-day registration.
register: You can register and vote through Election Day. Register by October 26 if you want a ballot mailed to you.
Only registered voters who live inside Boulder city limits get these city races.

key_dates.label: Vote Centers open for in-person voting
Last recommended day to return a ballot by mail
Election Day: ballots must be received by 7 p.m.

mayor.how: Rank the candidates: a 1st choice, then a 2nd, 3rd and so on if you want. You don't have to rank everyone.

council.how: Vote for up to five. The five candidates with the most votes win.

basics.rcv_count: If nobody has more than half the first-choice votes, the lowest candidate is eliminated and those ballots transfer to their next-ranked candidate still in the race; rounds continue until a winner is determined.
basics.scope: Only City of Boulder races and measures. Ballots also carry county, state, school board and regional items, which this guide does not cover.
